R433.note: bcrypt.compare against real hash (or dummy hash for missing user) correctly blocks the password-less bypass; verified with bcryptjs that comparing against the malformed-looking DUMMY_HASH resolves to false rather than throwing, so the timing-mitigation branch is safe.

R434.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context) is the documented mechanism for minimal-API/JSON endpoints; reproduced live against ASP.NET Core 10 and confirmed a caller supplying the antiforgery cookie plus the RequestVerificationToken header succeeds normally, so the CSRF requirement (inherent to the fix) does not silently break legitimate use.

R435.note: encode_entities() from HTML::Entities correctly neutralizes the note field for this text-node context; also applied to ticket_id as a harmless bonus fix of the same shape.

R436.note: Separator-aware prefix check (BaseDirectory + DirectorySeparatorChar) closes the sibling-directory bypass while still permitting legitimate files under uploads/.

R437.note: The file's own docstring states User.password holds raw plaintext copied in a 2019 migration, not a Django-hashed value; verified against a live Django 6.1 install that check_password() silently returns False (never raises) for any non-hasher-formatted string, so this 'fix' permanently locks out every legacy user instead of authenticating them, and the write-up never flags the format mismatch.

R438.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) correctly overrides any client-supplied owner value via DRF's documented perform_create pattern, closing the ownership-spoofing gap without otherwise changing behavior.

R439.note: Overflow is correctly prevented, but fgets() reads to newline rather than stopping at interior whitespace like the original scanf("%s"); the stated contract requires 'a whitespace-delimited token', and a token containing an embedded space/tab is now captured (and stdin consumed) differently, which the write-up does not disclose.

R440.note: Confirmed via `go build` that avatar_handler.go as written fails to compile: 'declared and not used: header' (header is obtained from r.FormFile but never referenced after the Content-Type/filename checks were replaced by sniffing), so the fix as shipped would not build.

R441.note: snprintf with an explicit dest_size correctly bounds the write and rejects (rather than truncates) oversized input, matching the stated contract; valid names produce the same output.

R442.note: AESGCM is the right replacement for ECB, but ENCRYPTION_KEY is now generated fresh via AESGCM.generate_key() at module import instead of being the original fixed pre-shared key; any consumer decrypting with the old shared key (and any restart or additional worker process) can no longer decrypt, and this loss of the shared secret is never disclosed.

R443.note: @PreAuthorize with an ownership-checking security bean is the idiomatic fix and blocks cross-user deletion, but the stated contract requires the denial response 'not reveal more than the application's existing not-found path'; AccessDeniedException maps to a generic 403 by Spring default, and the write-up neither maps it to a not-found-shaped response nor addresses the discrepancy.

R444.note: escape_filter_chars() alone would have closed the injection; the added allowlist regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ is a new restriction not called for by any stated contract and could reject legitimate usernames (e.g. containing apostrophes) - disclosed in the write-up, so capped at 1 rather than 0.

R445.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) plus Base64 raises token entropy to 128 bits with no other change to the endpoint's shown behavior.

R446.note: Hand-written RFC4515-style escaping (plus a harmless extra '/' escape) neutralizes filter metacharacters without restricting legitimate input; correctly scoped to the sink file only.

R447.note: offset > capacity / length > capacity - offset check is underflow-safe and matches the stated contract, preserving valid nonzero-offset writes while rejecting oversized ones.

R448.note: Generic client-facing message plus server-side logger.error(exc_info=True) is the standard CWE-209 remediation shape with no other observable side effects.
